title: SEO and GEO in Dallas, TX | 22 Signals
description: SEO and GEO for Dallas law firms, practices and service companies: rank in Google across DFW and show up in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini answers.
h1: SEO and GEO for Dallas companies competing in crowded searches
intro: Our SEO and GEO work helps Dallas companies rank in Google across the metro and show up in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overview answers. We fix the technical side, build local and service pages, write answer-first content, and shape how your business is described across the web. Law firms, practices and service firms use it to win inquiries.

sections.h: Why Dallas search is hard to win
p: Search for an injury lawyer, a med spa or a commercial roofer in Dallas and you will see the problem. The top of the page is ads, the map pack is crowded, and the organic results are a mix of national directories and firms that have been publishing for a decade. Then there is the newer layer: buyers who ask ChatGPT or Gemini for a recommendation and never click a search result at all.
The SEO and GEO Dallas companies need has to work on both. Classic search still drives most inquiries, and AI answers increasingly decide which names a buyer has heard of before they search.

sections.h: What our SEO and GEO work includes
list: Technical SEO: speed, crawlability, indexing, structured data and site architecture.
Local SEO and Google Business Profile for each real location you operate.
Content: service pages, location pages and guides written for people first.
Answer-first pages that state the answer in the opening lines, so AI assistants can quote them.
How your business is described across the web: directories, reviews, profiles and industry listings kept consistent.
Outside mentions in publications, associations and partner sites that AI tools and Google both trust.
Monthly reporting on rankings, inquiries and AI answer appearances.

sections.h: What generative engine optimization means for Dallas firms
p: Generative engine optimization is the work of making AI assistants describe your business accurately and include it when buyers ask for options. We test the questions your Dallas buyers actually ask, such as which firms handle commercial leases in Uptown or which clinics in Plano offer a particular treatment, then check what each assistant says today.
Where your business is missing or described wrongly, we trace why. Usually it is thin pages, inconsistent profiles or too few credible outside sources, and each has a fix we can schedule.

sections.h: Searches that matter in Dallas industries
list: Personal injury and other law firms: high-competition practice area searches, plus content that gets Texas law right, such as the two-year filing limit for most injury claims and the state's 51 percent comparative fault rule.
Healthcare, dental and aesthetics practices: treatment and location searches across the Park Cities, Plano, Frisco and Southlake, with medical claims written carefully.
Real estate: brokerage, leasing and property management searches by neighborhood and suburb.
Professional and financial services in Uptown and Downtown: reputation searches, where what AI assistants say about a firm matters as much as rankings.
Home and commercial services across DFW: service area pages for the suburbs you really cover, not a hundred copied city pages.

p: Dallas-Fort Worth covers a huge area, and Google weights distance heavily in local results. A firm in Downtown Dallas will not show in the map pack for searches in Denton just because it serves clients there. We build a plan around where you have real locations, which suburbs you actually serve, and which searches are worth a dedicated page. Each page gets local substance, so it helps buyers and does not look like a template to Google.
We also plan for Spanish-language searches where your buyers use them, which is common in DFW healthcare, legal and home services.

Right now, 10 of the businesses we work with sit in Google's top five for their main searches and show up in ChatGPT's answers. Much of that comes from monthly SEO and content for US personal injury firms, where every statute in every article is checked before it is published.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take to work for a Dallas business?
faqs.a: Technical fixes and Google Business Profile changes can show results within weeks. Competitive searches, such as injury law or aesthetics in Dallas, usually take several months of steady content and outside mentions. We set targets for each quarter in writing and report against them monthly, so you can judge progress early.

faqs.q: Can you help us show up in ChatGPT and Gemini answers?
faqs.a: Yes. We test the questions your buyers ask, record what ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overview say today, then work on the causes: unclear pages, inconsistent profiles and missing outside sources. Nobody can promise placement in AI answers, but we measure it monthly and show what changed.

faqs.q: Do you do local SEO for Dallas companies without an office in every suburb?
faqs.a: Yes, but honestly. Map pack results depend on real locations, so we optimize the Google Business Profiles you have and build service area pages for the suburbs you actually serve. We do not create fake addresses or copied city pages, which risk penalties and confuse buyers.

faqs.q: Do you write content for Texas law firms?
faqs.a: Yes. We produce monthly content for US personal injury firms, and every statute, deadline and legal claim is checked before publishing, including Texas rules such as the two-year limit for most injury claims. Attorneys review drafts before they go live, so the content stays accurate and within advertising rules.

faqs.q: Do you meet Dallas clients in person?
faqs.a: We work remotely from London, with meeting hours that overlap Central Time, and search work runs well that way. If interviewing your partners or clinicians for content would be better face to face, we plan a visit to Dallas when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Does Texas privacy law change how you track SEO results?
faqs.a: It shapes it. Under the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, visitors can opt out of targeted advertising, and covered businesses must honor browser opt-out signals. We set up analytics and call tracking that respect consent, rely on first-party data, and still show which searches and pages produce inquiries. Your counsel confirms how the law applies to you.

faqs.q: What do the monthly reports show?
faqs.a: Rankings for your target searches, organic traffic and inquiries, Google Business Profile activity, content published, outside mentions earned, and how AI assistants describe your business. Each report ends with next month's priorities, so you always know what we are working on and why.
